title: Chapter 8 — Your First 90 Days
intro: The structured ramp from day one to certified floor professional. What to learn, when to learn it, and how to know you are on track.

sections.title: Days 1-30: Learn the Floor
sections.content:
Your first month is about absorbing — not selling. Learn the showroom layout. Learn where every product category lives. Learn the brands your store carries and what makes each one different.

Walk the floor every day. Open every refrigerator door. Pull out every drawer. Turn on every range. You need to know these products physically, not just from a spec sheet.

Shadow the top performers. Watch how they greet customers. Listen to their discovery questions. Notice how they demonstrate products. You are building a mental library of what good looks like.

By the end of month one, you should be able to walk a customer through any section of the showroom without getting lost or looking uncertain.

sections.title: Days 31-60: Start Selling with Support
sections.content:
Month two is where you start applying the 10 Steps with real customers — but with a safety net. Your manager or a mentor should be nearby to support you.

Focus on the first five steps: Engagement, Rapport, Discovery, Needs Assessment, and Wants Assessment. These are where most new salespeople struggle — not because they are hard, but because they require patience. The temptation is to skip straight to showing product. Resist it.

You will lose some sales. That is normal. Every lost sale teaches you something if you are paying attention. After each customer interaction, ask yourself: which of the 10 Steps did I miss? What would I do differently?

sections.title: Days 61-90: Own Your Process
sections.content:
Month three is where you become independent. You should be running the full 10 Steps on your own — engagement through follow-up — with increasing confidence.

Start building your CRM. Every customer you work gets logged. Every follow-up gets scheduled. This is the beginning of your personal database — the asset that will compound for your entire career.

By day 90, you should be able to: greet a customer without triggering their defences, complete a thorough discovery, recommend the right product with confidence, demonstrate it effectively, handle basic objections, ask for the sale directly, and follow up within 24 hours.

You will not be perfect. But you should be professional, consistent, and improving every week.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating a new salesperson's 90-day ramp, ask:

Do they know the showroom layout and product categories?
Can they run through all 10 Steps — even if they are not smooth yet?
Are they logging customers in the CRM from day one?
Are they shadowing top performers and asking questions?
Are they improving week over week — or repeating the same mistakes?
Do they show the drive and curiosity that predicts long-term success?

The first 90 days do not predict someone's ceiling. They reveal whether the person has the habits and attitude to keep climbing.
